newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico peso claws back lost ground in late trade.
newsitem.headline: Mexico peso claws back lost ground in late trade.

text.p: The Mexican benchmark 48-hour peso was 0.5 of a centavo weaker at 7.350/7.5450 per dollar in late trade on Tuesday, after what traders said had been a volatile session.

The 48-hour contract had been three centavos weaker at one stage, but traders said the relative recovery was due to dealers dumping surplus dollar positions acquired in speculative early trade, a move fueled by prospects that primary rates would soar at this evening's auction of Cetes Treasury bills.
Money market traders said they expected bellwether 28-day Cetes rates to rise by some 400 basis points.
